newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA AUTO AGREES UNION WAGE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA AUTO AGREES UNION WAGE DEAL.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, Skoda Automobilova a.s., said on Tuesday it had agreed with its unions to raise wages an average of 10.1 percent this year, the company said in a statement.
"In the framework of negotiations of a collective agreement the management of (Skoda) settled with the leadership of the trade union Kovo," it said.
Skoda's unions had issued indefinite strike warnings if a new collective agreement for 1997 was not reached soon.
Skoda said that the pay rises reflected expected increases in the cost of living, and brought 1997 union wages to a range of 6,438-19,856 crowns per month.
The company is the largest Czech car maker and the country's largest single industrial exporter. Volkswagen took majority control of Skoda in 1995.
Czech inflation slowed in January to 7.4 percent year-on-year from 8.6 percent in December, but was influenced by price deregulations and tax changes at the beginning of 1996.
